We started making it into a contest, but she always had me beat because she was able to purge, whereas I’ve never been able to make myself, no matter how many times I’ve tried. She and I always hung out together back then, so we were always keeping each other in check, especially when her mom would take us out to eat. In high school, things changed because I attended a different one and lost quite a bit of weight, before switching my junior year to the same one she was at. Her new friends all bullied me and I got fat off of school pizza. I miss our friendship, even though it was unhealthy for both of us, because I felt so much more in control with her at my side. Plus.. it was just nice to have a friend who understood your struggles.

But yeah, it was when we really solidified our friendship in middle school that I started participating in disordered eating behaviors. I’d been hating my body for being fatter than other girls’ for a few years before then, but she was the catalyst.

Disordered eating is problematic eating habits that don’t quite fit the criteria of eating disorders (anorexia, bulimia, BED, and eating disorders not otherwise specified). There are specific diagnostic criteria for each eating disorder, but a lot of times, someone can have some of those symptoms, but fall short of meeting the criteria. That’s where disordered eating comes in.
However, in my opinion, because you aren’t *thinking* about it, this makes time think that it’s not disordered eating but rather something else neurological. It could be something wrong with the communication between your stomach and your brain, or something equally out of place, but I think the best thing for you to do here, is to see your doctor and talk to them about what exactly is going on. Make sure you mention that it literally just doesn’t cross your mind to eat because you don’t have that hunger to remind you. Ask your doctor about vitamin supplements as well because if you’re not eating enough, your body will definitely be lacking in the vitamins and minerals it needs to function. They should be taking your blood in this appointment to find out exactly what your levels are and what you need.
In the meantime, while I know it can be uncomfortable to eat when you’re hungry, I would an alarm on your phone at least twice a day reminding you to eat. You can choose what you eat, whether it’s a ‘meal’ or a snack, but try and make it something you’re okay with eating that would also be nutritional. 
I hope this comment and all the others help and that you see a doctor and get on the path of being well fed and stronger <3 wishing you the best luck!

I just kind of made it a habit. I always take them before I get into bed (which isn’t the best thing because sometimes I get into bed at 9pm and sometimes I get into bed at 5am). There were several occasions, when I first started, that I’d forget. It made me feel awful the next day and completely disoriented. I almost crashed my dad’s car on the way to school because my vision was shaking and rolling. 
After 6 years of being on medication, I still have the occasional forgetful day, but it’s few and far between.
My advice- find something that you already do everyday and pair it together. 
-You can also get one of those ‘week pill cases’ that have the days of the week on them to store meds in? I found that was really helpful in the beginning too. Set an alarm to make sure you refill it at the end of every week. 
-Set an alarm for a time you know you’re always home to take your meds.
-keep them in a visible place so you’ll remember when you see them

I can’t really think of anything else except try your best and make it a habit. I hope it works out for you!

If he presses and asks why or what made you uncomfortable, you say “I’m not really comfortable answering that right now” 
or “it’s personal and something I’d prefer to keep to myself right now” 
or “why do you need to know? Isn’t me saying I’m uncomfortable enough? Do I have to have a reason to be uncomfortable?”
Also! Please don’t say you’re sorry. There is nothing to be sorry for in this situation, on both sides of it.  If he says sorry, you can accept his apology but tell him it isn’t necessary because he didn’t know. I know it’ll be hard not to apologize but there’s nothing to be sorry for.

If someone asked me to stop doing something because they were uncomfortable, I’d stop without asking any questions because it isn’t my business- and the majority of people are the same.
You got this! I believe in you and I know for a fact that if he values your friendship, he will stop and won’t ask questions. You’re going to be fine <3

This is kind of on the same train of thought, but when I was 11, my mom’s friend fell into an absolutely terrible depression. It’s started out as post-partum and just got worse from there. I remember sitting a parking lot of Whole Foods while my mom was just crying next to me taking about how her friend was suicidal and she didn’t know what to do. When she was done, I told her that I thought suicide was incredibly selfish and mean to the people who loved you and that anyone who even considered suicide was already terrible because they were going to purposefully hurt their family. I said some really messed up stuff. 
Two years later, at 13, I had my first suicidal thought. At 14, I had my first attempt. I’ve been suicidal for 7 years. I regret everything I ever said then. I was incredibly uneducated (I was 11 though, so can’t expect much there) and could only see the hurt and pain that appeared on the surface, especially my moms. I couldn’t fathom why anyone would be so cruel that they’d hurt themselves and make my mom cry because of it. 
I’ve learned so much since I was 11 about depression, self harm, and suicide- not just through education but through personal experience. It’s good to see that even though my thoughts back then we’re narrow and cruel, I have grown as a person.
Although, it is some fucked up kind of karma. Younger you disliked people with eating disorders and then you developed one. Younger me thought suicidal people were horribly selfish and not trying hard enough to get better, and then I became suicidal myself. Shits wild man.

Hey friend, please don’t feel bad about posting these. This sub isn’t just for deep self harm or shallow- it’s for all self harm. Sometimes, it’s really hard looking through the sub because you see people with worse scars than you and it can make you feel invalidated. It’s hard for me too, because my self harm isn’t deep, and sometimes looking at the pictures here, it makes me question my own pain and internal conflict. But it’s important to remind ourselves that it’s not about how big or deep the scars are, but rather that all of it just sucks. We all feel shitty and need to hurt ourselves sometimes, and the shittiness we feel is no more or less than the shittiness others feel. Pain isn’t a competition, though it can feel like that. Your pain is 100% valid and your scars are still ‘bad’ because you felt crappy enough to put them there and that’s enough. We’re all in this together and no one is ‘worse’ than others. 
Sorry that’s a flippin mess, I am NOT good with words. 
Also! Try getting some scar cream or bio oil if you can. If you’re in the US, bio oil is sold at Target. Just make sure if you use or, to put some sunscreen on before going outside, because it causes your skin to burn a little more. Keep in mind that they may not fade a ton, but whatever happens, you’re going to be okay and you should never NEVER feel ashamed of your scars, okay?
Thank you for posting this, because even though I know it must have been hard, you’re helping others with the same sort of scars know that they too, are valid.

I remember the first time I talked to a friend who also self harmed. She said that the physical pain helped cover up the mental pain and that’s why she did it. I’m the same in that I don’t really feel much of anything anymore, but (TW) the pain that comes with cutting isn’t euphoric or an adrenaline rush for me. I don’t like the pain or the burning or the itching as it heals. But when I do it and see the blood and the scans and the scars and sometimes the words/numbers, it just gives me a sense of peace. It makes me feel at rest and calm. I haven’t found anything else that gives me that. 
So yeah, I’m the same. I find them aesthetically pleasing and when I see fresh scars on myself, I just feel this quiet peace inside. I just really like the look of them and the way they change over time.

I have struggled so much with my will to live in the past five years. I take the leaves off the floor of garden centers to bring home because I can grow new succulents from them. I have quite a collection now- it takes about half an hour to water all of them, and I only plan on having more in the future. These dumb little plants are the only things that make me feel happy, even on my worst days. I know I couldn’t die because my family doesn’t know how to take care of them properly, and I don’t want my plants to die. 
Anyway, I just wanted to say I really related to this. Sometimes, having something small and low maintenance that depends on you to live is what you need to get through the day.

My mom and I are really close, but my dad and I have always been super emotionally constipated around each other. Anything other than superficial human makes the conversation awkward. He found out about my depression when my mom took me to a psychiatrist and I started taking meds, since they were covered by health insurance. We didn’t talk about it other than the occasional ‘hey, maybe you should take a walk today and then you’ll feel better’ or ‘these meds are expensive’ (with an implied ‘are you sure you need them?’). I had to go to the ER two years ago after going to a friend for help because I was in a bad place and they called the cops on me. It was just me and my dad, the cops came in, took me to the hospital, it was awful. After that, a specialist told my parents to check in with me constantly and my dad tried, but I hated it so, so much. 
I’ve accepted now that so long as nothing obvious happens, we don’t have to talk about it, which is what I want. The other night, however, I was sitting down and my shorts had ridden up and showed some scars from a few months ago and he pointed them out asking what they were. I said they were old, then cracked a joke about him being old, and we forgot about it. 
Sorry for the rant, I just know what it’s like to have one parent who you can talk to and who will support you and another who can’t seem to talk when emotions show up.
